compiled_state.title: FP-RECOVERY-WORKFLOW.md: review dispatch -> primes reviewer with prior finding + FP suspicion, biasing toward clearance
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior
FP-recovery's review sub-agent should receive the SAME neutral standard code review prompt as the commit/local workflow — no knowledge of the prior CI finding or the FP suspicion. A true false positive then does not reappear (trustworthy clearance); a legitimate concern is independently re-raised and must be resolved.

#### Actual Behavior
FP-RECOVERY-WORKFLOW.md Step 2's dispatch template injected an `=== ISSUE CONTEXT ===` block naming the suspected FP and pasting the CI finding verbatim, plus the engineer's rationale. This primes the reviewer toward confirming the FP / clearing — and could rubber-stamp a *legitimate* finding into a bypass, undermining the escape valve's integrity. Empirically (PR #676): a primed dispatch and a neutral dispatch on the identical diff both returned 0 findings, but only the neutral run is trustworthy because it is unconditioned.

### 7. Additional Details
Fix: neutralize the Step 2 dispatch (diff only, no finding/FP context); add a HARD-GATE + verdict semantics (a neutral re-raise = legitimate, not re-litigation). Files: plugins/dso/docs/workflows/FP-RECOVERY-WORKFLOW.md, plugins/dso/skills/fp-recovery/SKILL.md. detected_by:internal-dogfood inferred — surfaced while dogfooding fp-recovery on PR #676 this session.
